To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) OSNs housed in basiconic sensilla respond to plant odors, whereas those in long-trichoids respond to female-produced sex-pheromone components; (2) OSN sensitivity and temporal characteristics are spatially organized along the antenna, with OSNs in the more proximal segments of the antenna being more sensitive and having shorter latency and more phasic responses than OSNs in the distal segment.

the spatial organization of antennal OSNs in the moth S. littoralis is associated with differences in sensitivity, temporal characteristics, and specificity, which are likely to be important for the moth's ability to detect and discriminate among odors.
the antennal olfactory system in the moth Spodoptera littorals is organized spatially, with OSNs in the proximal antenna being more sensitive than those in the distal antenna.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional organization of OSN populations in the antenna of the polyphagous noctuid moth, Spodoptera littorals.
the spatial distribution, sensitivity, and response diversity of olfactory sensory neurons housed in antennal sensilla.
the spatial organization and temporal characteristics of olfactory sensilla on the antennae of female moths.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antennae of the female S. littoralis moth are equipped with a large number of olfactory receptor neurons that can be grouped into 32 functional sensilla types.
the antennal OSNs in S. littoralis are tuned for a broad array of plant volatiles and that OSNs in basicoic and long-trichoid are tuned for the female sex phermonones.
in this moth, the OSNs are spatially organized, with a clear proximodistal variation in sensitivity and temporal coding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the antennae of S. littoralis are equipped with OSNs that respond to plant and female sex phero- mone odors, with some differences in their sensitivity and temporal characteristics, and that the OSNs in the different sensilla types show different response profiles to the tested stimuli.

the antennae of the polyphagous female S. littoralis moth contain a diverse array of OSNs, with different temporal characteristics and sensitivities, that may contribute to a broad range of olfactory behaviors.
OSN diversity is not only determined by the number of different OSN types present, but also by the number of OSNs within each OSN type.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spatial arrangement of OSNs on the antenna of a generalist herbivore is not random and that this arrangement is likely to have functional consequences for the moth's behavior.
OSN spatial arrangement in antennae is a key element of olfactory processing.
the antennal olfactory system of S. littoralis has a high diversity in OSN response characteristics, which may be related to the broad host range of this moth.
